for the weights,
due dates,
and where to submit each one.

## Why this page exists

These five tasks are small,
they are each worth the same 1%,
and they are easy to miss because no two of them are submitted the same way.

They are listed here so that everything you owe in this course
is in the one place you already look.
Canvas remains the place with the actual links and instructions.
This page tells you what each one is.

Note that these are due **mid-week**,
not the usual Saturday 6 PM.
Week 1 is front-loaded on purpose,
so that anything broken on your machine turns up
before Milestone 1 is due at the end of the week.

## Setup

Install the MDS software stack and confirm it works.

Do this one first.
Everything else in Week 1 assumes your machine is working,
and this is the task that finds out whether it is.

## Policies

Read the program policies and answer the questions on PrairieLearn.

This is also your first time using PrairieLearn,
which you will meet again in the weekly practice questions
and in a graded setting in another course.

## Student information survey

A short survey allowing teaching team to gather you github usernames and other necessary info for subsequent courses. Find it on PrairieLearn.

## Lab 0a: Python and Lab 0b: R

Two short labs covered during the orientation (find the recording in pins of the course slack channel),
one per language.

They check that your Python and R installations
can actually run and submit work.
They do not check whether you already know the languages.

[JupyterLab orientation chapter](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/jupyterlab-orientation-intro.html) and [RStudio orientation chapter](https://ubc-mds.github.io/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/lectures/rstudio-orientation-intro.html) will be helpful for these labs.

:::{.callout-warning}
